target.title: fix(extensions): bound success-path JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three success-path response reads still used unbounded `response.json()` / `resp.json()`. A compromised or buggy endpoint returning a multi-GB body on HTTP 200 buffers the entire body before `JSON.parse` even runs, OOMing the agent. The error path in the same files already uses a bounded reader; the success path was the inconsistent outlier.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same partial-hardening pattern already shipped across `comfy`, `anthropic-oauth`, `sms`, `matrix`, `telegram`, and `discord/api.ts` (`b1fae752f8`, `bf66b4e1ea`, `6e98477ee4`, `853a274f14`). The three remaining sites are the obvious next batch (the other two sites in the source triage — minimax/oauth and mattermost/client — were already bounded on `main`).

## User Impact

No behavior change for well-formed responses (small, valid JSON still parses). A huge or non-JSON success body is now truncated at a cap and handled gracefully instead of buffering in full and OOMing. `thread-ownership` (409 conflict body), `discord` webhook (`{id, channel_id}`), and `huggingface` model discovery (`/v1/models`) all apply the same `readResponseTextLimited` + `JSON.parse` pattern already used by their error paths.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The success-path `response.json()` / `resp.json()` reads buffered the entire response body with no size cap, so a huge body could OOM before parsing.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `2256a7d21b` on branch `fix/unbounded-success-json-reads`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-bounded-json-reads.mjs` — imports the real `readResponseTextLimited` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http` (the helper now used by all three patched sites) and exercises it over real `Response` objects: a small valid body, and a 10 MB body.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-bounded-json-reads.mjs
  [small valid body] read 19 bytes; JSON.parse -> owner=agent-1

  [huge 10MB body] read capped at 65536 bytes (full body was 10485760 bytes)
  truncated -> JSON.parse: SyntaxError (caller catch handles -> fallback)

  [contrast] response.text()/json() buffers full 10485760 bytes (the OOM pattern this PR removes)

  Verdict: success-path body reads are now capped at the limit; a huge body no longer buffers in full (OOM mitigated)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** A 10 MB success body is read only up to the cap (65 536 bytes) instead of buffering in full; the truncated text fails `JSON.parse` and each site's new try/catch handles it (`discord` webhook -> `{}` as before; `huggingface` -> bundled catalog, matching the `!response.ok` branch; `thread-ownership` -> propagates to its existing try/finally). A small valid body still parses cleanly.
- **What was not tested:** A live huge response from each real upstream (the real `readResponseTextLimited` helper over real `Response` objects is the faithful unit; each patched site now calls it instead of `response.json()`).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/thread-ownership/index.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)      Tests  21 passed (21)
$ pnpm test extensions/huggingface/models.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)      Tests   8 passed (8)
$ pnpm test extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.proxy.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)      Tests  (3 shards, all passed)
```

No new test added: the success-path behavior is unchanged for well-formed responses (existing suites pass), and the bound is provided by the already-tested shared `readResponseTextLimited` helper; the node runtime verification above proves the cap is now applied to these reads.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended, bounded) - a huge/non-JSON success body is now truncated + handled instead of buffering in full; well-formed responses unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: Yes (improvement) - bounds response-body reads on three success paths, mitigating OOM from a compromised/buggy upstream; no new credential, network, or command-execution path.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) - touches three extensions (thread-ownership, discord, huggingface); each uses the shared `readResponseTextLimited` helper already used by its own error path. No public/plugin SDK API change.
- Highest-risk area: a legitimately large-but-valid success body that exceeds the cap would now fall back (webhook -> {}, huggingface -> bundled catalog). All three success payloads are tiny in practice (well under 8-64 KB), and the prior behavior for an over-large body was an OOM crash, so the fallback is strictly safer.
- Mitigation: existing thread-ownership (21) + huggingface models (8) + discord webhook (3 shards) tests pass + node runtime verification proving the cap is applied.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
